overview: The Committee of the Whole held its seventh preliminary budget meeting for fiscal year 2027 to review the Mayor's overview and specific departmental budgets. The council focused on a $2.18 million funding gap for public schools, legal expenditure transparency, and staffing levels across the Police and Public Works departments.

items.title: Mayor's FY27 Budget Presentation
items.summary: Mayor Lungo-Koehn presented a $218.2 million general fund budget, emphasizing investments in infrastructure, climate resiliency, and Medford Square redevelopment. She noted that rising health insurance, pensions, and special education transportation continue to place significant pressure on the operating budget.

items.title: Council Discussion on Funding Gaps and Staffing
items.summary: Councilors expressed frustration over the late delivery of major department budgets and discussed potential solutions for a $240,000 deficit in the Medford Family Network. Discussion also addressed the need for competitive library staff pay, recruitment for a city solicitor, and long-term revenue forecasting for new developments.

items.title: Review of Legal Costs and KP Law Services
items.summary: The council debated the transparency of legal expenses, which are currently distributed across various departmental professional service lines. The administration defended the current costs as lower than peer cities and highlighted successful litigation defense, while the council requested a centralized report on all legal settlements and vendor fees.

items.title: Parking Department Budget Review
items.summary: Director McDermod reported that citation revenue exceeded $1.7 million by the end of April, marking a significant increase in productivity over the previous year. The department is preparing an RFP for a new parking management system to address resident complaints and improve merchant processing fee structures.

items.title: Medford Police and Traffic Division Budget Review
items.summary: The police budget increased by over 17% due to the implementation of settled collective bargaining agreements covering multiple years of retroactive raises. Officials discussed the impact of staffing shortages on the traffic division and the department's goal to reach 105 funded positions to reduce reliance on forced overtime.

items.title: Medford Public Schools Budget Review
items.summary: The school administration presented a $89.9 million budget, noting a $2.18 million gap between projected needs and the Mayor's preliminary allocation. A significant disagreement remains between school and city officials over whether $2.1 million in override stabilization funds should be counted toward the recurring permanent base budget.

items.title: Department of Public Works Budget Review
items.summary: Director McGivern highlighted progress on lead service line removal and the deployment of an in-house paving crew funded by the override. Discussion included a $10.5 million waste disposal contract, a new urban forest management plan, and the challenges of retaining specialized mechanics at municipal pay scales.
